name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -19 point partisan lean
Incumbent Dan Meuser running for reeption with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price the Democrat at only about 3%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's -19 point Republican lean, Meuser's incumbency and roughly 3-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets pricing his win near 96% all point to a safe Republican hold. With no polling or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or an unexpectedly strong Democratic fundraising surge could move this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dan Meuser seeks another term in a northeastern Pennsylvania district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan advantage of about 19 points for the GOP. He has raised roughly $1.9 million to Rachel Wallace's $700,000, though Wallace holds more cash on hand. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race, and no public polls or expert ratings are available.

Prediction markets give Meuser about a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals, incumbency, and money all align with a comfortable Republican victory, and the forecast expects a margin in the high teens for Meuser.
